Here are the extracted quantitative parameters and values from the text:

1. Less than 10% of the DCs in the draining lymph nodes produced pMHC class II complexes.
2. Ovalbumin-specific T cells formed small clusters around fluorescent DCs in draining lymph nodes 24 hours after subcutaneous injection of fluorochrome-labeled ovalbumin.
3. Ovalbumin-specific T cells were found adjacent to bead-containing DCs in peribronchial lymph nodes 12 hours after beads were given intranasally.
4. Real-time microscope imaging showed that antigen-specific T cells form clusters 32 hours after exposure to subcutaneously injected soluble antigen.
